questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$\theta$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=0, xmax=380, ymin=-1.35, ymax=1.35,
  xtick={90,180,270,360}, minor x tick num=2,
  ytick={-1,-0.5,0.5,1},
  xmajorgrids, xminorgrids, ymajorgrids, grid style={gray!25},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=7cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:360] {cos(x)};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The graph shown starts at $(0,1)$ and first reaches $0$ at $90^{\circ}$.
Which trigonometric function is it?

options.why: $y=\sin\theta$ starts at $(0,0)$, not $(0,1)$.
$y=\tan\theta$ has asymptotes and no maximum; this curve is a smooth bounded wave.
$y=-\cos\theta$ would start at $(0,-1)$, but this graph starts at $(0,1)$.

questions.solution_text:
A smooth wave starting at $(0,1)$ and falling to $0$ at $90^{\circ}$ is the cosine curve.
This is $y=\cos\theta$.

Use the graph of $y=\cos\theta$ to find the values of $\theta$ in $0^{\circ}\le\theta<360^{\circ}$ where $\cos\theta=0.5$.

options.why: Gave only the first solution; the cosine curve also equals $0.5$ at $300^{\circ}$.
These are where $\cos\theta=-0.5$, not $+0.5$.
The second angle should be $360^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=300^{\circ}$, not $180^{\circ}+60^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
Draw the line $y=0.5$ and read where it meets the cosine curve.
It crosses at $\theta=60^{\circ}$ and $\theta=300^{\circ}$.

options.why: $180^{\circ}$ is the period of $\tan\theta$, not $\cos\theta$.
$90^{\circ}$ is the shift between sine and cosine, not the period.
One full wave of $\cos\theta$ completes in $360^{\circ}$, not $720^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
The cosine curve completes one full wave and repeats every $360^{\circ}$.
The period is $360^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y=\sin\theta$ is an odd function, so $\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta$.
Given that $\sin40^{\circ}\approx0.64$, what is $\sin(-40^{\circ})$?

options.why: Treated $\sin\theta$ as even; it is odd, so $\sin(-40^{\circ})=-\sin40^{\circ}$.
Used $\cos40^{\circ}\approx0.77$ and dropped the sign; the question is about $\sin$.
Used $\cos40^{\circ}\approx0.77$ instead of $\sin40^{\circ}$.

Using the period of $y=\cos\theta$, how many solutions does $\cos\theta=-1$ have in $0^{\circ}\le\theta\le720^{\circ}$?

options.why: Counted only $\theta=180^{\circ}$ and missed the repeat at $540^{\circ}$ one period later.
Counted as if $\cos\theta=-1$ occurred twice per cycle; the minimum $-1$ is reached once per $360^{\circ}$.
Included an angle where $\cos\theta=1$, such as $0^{\circ}$ or $360^{\circ}$, which is the maximum, not $-1$.

questions.solution_text:
$\cos\theta=-1$ at the minimum of each cycle, once every $360^{\circ}$.
In $0^{\circ}\le\theta\le720^{\circ}$ that is at $\theta=180^{\circ}$ and $\theta=540^{\circ}$.
So there are $2$ solutions.

questions.question_text: In the equation $y=5\sin x-2$, what is the maximum $y$ value?

options.why: Uses the vertical translation alone and ignores the positive sine amplitude.
Adds the amplitude and translation incorrectly instead of calculating $5(1)-2$.
Subtracts the translation from the amplitude with the wrong numerical result.

questions.solution_text: Because $-1\leq\sin x\leq1$, the maximum occurs when $\sin x=1$. Thus $y_{\max}=5(1)-2=3$.
